language.script_notes: Yucatec Maya is widely spoken and appears on some signs and place names (x, dz and double vowels — Xcaret, Dzibilchaltún, Chicxulub).

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam on the Mérida–Cancún toll road; little elsewhere — the terrain is flat and there is nothing to fall off.
road_furniture.line_paint: White and yellow lines on the main roads; long dead-straight roads through flat scrub jungle. 'Topes' at every village.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs in towns; pale limestone gravel shoulders.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Octagonal or crucifix concrete poles. OXXO in the towns; heavy tourist and hotel signage along the Quintana Roo coast; roadside Maya ruins.

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs with tinacos in towns; rounded thatched roofs on traditional Maya houses.
architecture.roof_material: Concrete slab; palm or guano thatch on Maya 'na' houses; resort tile and concrete on the coast.
architecture.wall_construction: Block and rendered masonry; whitewashed colonial buildings in Mérida; traditional oval Maya houses with rounded ends and stick or stone walls; large gated resort and condo developments along the Riviera Maya.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewash and pastels in Mérida; bright colours in villages; manicured beige resort palettes on the coast.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Oval Maya thatched houses with rounded ends; pastel colonial Mérida; henequen-hacienda ruins; Maya archaeological sites (Chichén Itzá, Uxmal, Tulum); wall-to-wall tourist development from Cancún to Tulum.

nature.vegetation: Low, dense, fairly uniform dry scrub-jungle over almost the whole peninsula; old henequen (agave) fields; mangroves and coconut palms along the Caribbean coast.
nature.terrain: Dead flat limestone shelf — no hills except the low Puuc ridge in the south, and no rivers or surface streams at all; water sits in sinkholes (cenotes). Soil and roads are pale limestone white.
nature.climate_signature: Hot and humid year-round, hurricane-prone. The total flatness, the absence of rivers, the pale white ground and the even low canopy are the giveaway.

vehicles.plate_color: State plates for Yucatán, Quintana Roo and Campeche, each with its own design.
vehicles.plate_format: State-dependent, commonly three letters and three–four digits.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Three-wheeled mototaxis are the standard transport in small towns; rental cars and tour vans around the Riviera Maya.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage on the highways and the tourist coast; long identical straight roads through flat jungle in between.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat low jungle continues straight across the border; right-hand traffic; similar climate and Maya ruins
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Belize is English-speaking with British-style signage and its own plates; Mexico's Yucatán has Spanish signs, Mexican state plates, OXXO and 'topes'.
Guatemalan plates and rougher roads; no OXXO; the Petén is more forested and less developed than the Yucatán's toll-road-and-resort corridor.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — ALTO, OXXO, tinacos, state plates
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Yucatán is perfectly flat with white limestone ground, no rivers, uniform low jungle and Maya round houses; central Mexico is a mountainous plateau with volcanoes and colonial cities.
